PARADE_RULES: Ninety minutes to build. Anything in the garage, inventory, or safe room is material. A procession can be any length and any number of floats.
Five groups, five themes, one word each. Express it visually and performatively.
The route is three kilometers of yellow-brick road with knee-high fog. Spectators line the whole thing and cannot attack.
The Judging Stands are at roughly two kilometers; each group performs there once.
The tenth floor's vehicle rules are gone. No magical repair, no consumable refresh. Fix it by hand or don't.
The route ends in an arena stocked with tenth-floor mobs, former crawlers (or substitutes), and the floor boss. The stairwell opens when the boss dies.
Total floor time: three hours and fifteen minutes. The staging area is a safe room until the parade starts.
PARADE_BOSS_MECHANICS: Only damaged while a float is intact within the arena; the floats are the weak points and it knows it.
Summons a wave of former crawlers each time it loses a quarter of its health.
Breaks the arena floor in stages; the fighting ring shrinks.
Silences spells while the crowd is chanting; kill the noise or fight in it.
Takes a parade theme each phase and becomes it.
Cannot be killed while the Grand Master lives. The Grand Master is in the stands.

COLLAPSE_NOTES: Days ago, every structure on Earth larger than a shed folded downward into the ground in perfect unison — the Collapse. Anyone caught inside a falling building died instantly; anyone caught outside, in a basement, or in the open woke to find the wreckage gone and a dungeon in its place.

The Collapse took every building on the planet at once, without warning, and without survivors inside them. What's left of humanity entered the dungeon that swallowed the wreckage, because the alternative — the open, monster-infested surface — was worse.
The System harvested Earth's buildings in the Collapse and replaced them with this dungeon. Everyone who wasn't standing in a doorway, a basement, or open ground when it happened is simply gone.
TUTORIAL_GUILD_BLURB: Runs the crawler tutorial: interface, inventory, loot boxes, stats, and the media economy that rewards being watched as much as being skilled.
Offers race and class guidance, potion-brewing services, and a blunt explanation of why survival and spectacle are the same skill down here.
Explains achievements, followers, and patrons to anyone who walks in, whether or not they asked.
